claim: In provisioned mode, the capacity limits of a Kinesis data stream are defined by its number of shards. While they are exceeded, put data calls are rejected with a ProvisionedThroughputExceeded exception. If this is due to a temporary rise in the stream input data rate, retries by the producer eventually complete the requests. If the rise is sustained, increase the number of shards so the put calls consistently succeed.

qualifiers.condition: put data calls rejected with ProvisionedThroughputExceeded because the capacity limits are exceeded

evidence.quote: In provisioned mode, the capacity limits of a Kinesis data stream are defined by the number of shards within the data stream. The limits can be exceeded either by data throughput or by the number of PUT records. While the capacity limits are exceeded, the put data call will be rejected with a ProvisionedThroughputExceeded exception.

If this is due to a temporary rise of the data stream’s input data rate, retry by the data producer will eventually lead to completion of the requests. If it’s due to a sustained rise of the data stream’s input data rate, you should increase the number of shards within your data stream to provide enough capacity for the put data calls to consistently succeed.
